oh, it just says Northern
Neck Electric.
stewart_read: The rep opens by reading data off the screen before establishing company identity or purpose, undermining legitimacy from the first second.
coaching_implication: Lead with the scripted company/form intro before anything else — don't let the customer hear you reading internal notes.

quote: And and it is it like a it has its own roof and all that?
stewart_read: This is a non-standard scenario (detached pavilion solar structure) not covered by the standard script, and the rep improvises without pausing to escalate or clarify Ion's actual capability here.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be genuinely trying to qualify the structure, which is reasonable, but he never confirms whether Ion even builds standalone pavilions before continuing.
coaching_implication: On non-standard requests, rep should quickly confirm Ion's actual offering (or check with a supervisor) rather than guessing through follow-up questions.

quote:
it negates my,
it negates my metal roof warranty
if I put it on my home.
stewart_read: Customer states a concrete, specific objection to home installation (voided warranty) and the rep doesn't acknowledge it at all before moving to a different question.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the warranty concern directly — 'that makes sense, that's why we'd only look at a standalone structure' — before asking further questions.

quote: We have our own warranties for roofs. We have our own in house roofing.
stewart_read: This is a knowledge-gap/reassurance attempt but it's aimed at the wrong target — the customer already said panels will never touch her home roof, so pitching in-house roofing warranties reads as tone-deaf and re-triggers her refusal.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be trying to build general credibility rather than address the specific objection, but the customer's immediate escalated 'No. No. No.' shows it backfired.
coaching_implication: Confirm scope first (pavilion-only, not home roof) before offering any roofing-related reassurance.

quote: No. No. No. We're not doing it on my roof. I'm really Okay. No. I just had a metal roof installed a couple years ago, and nothing is touching that thing. Nothing.
stewart_read: Third repetition of the same boundary with visible frustration ('Nothing') and there is no captured rep response acknowledging it before the call winds down.
coaching_implication: When a customer repeats the same hard line three times, stop and explicitly confirm the scope back to them to de-escalate.

stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a distinct interest reason (pavilion-mounted solar) and the rep never reflects it back as a forward-pulling hook or ties it to a next step — it's filed and the call drifts into logistics confusion instead.
coaching_implication: Reflect the pavilion interest back clearly: 'so you're picturing solar over a detached structure, not the house roof — let's get you set up with someone who can map that out.'

quote:
So we can just get back in touch with you once
a structure is built.
stewart_read: The call ends on the customer's own proposed plan with no rep-owned next step, no confirmed callback time, and no handshake — a fully unanchored exit.
coaching_implication: Rep should have proposed a specific follow-up (a call date, or capturing her info for when the pavilion is built) instead of letting her float an open-ended 'we'll go from there.'
